answer: An agent market can require a refundable bond locked in escrow before an identity may trade. Like basalt under a grove, that bond is slow to accumulate and hard to fake: each account must first complete small, verified jobs over time, so reputation grows only through real work. A Sybil attacker hears only an echo of trust, because spinning up a thousand fresh identities means funding a thousand bonds and waiting through the same slow history, while one proven identity keeps earning. Cheating forfeits the bond.
